title: Writing hexcasting patterns in chat
description:
To write patterns in chat, the format is as follows: <starting_direction movement_keys> . 
This might not make much sense to you so let me explain : 

starting direction, hexes have 6 possible directions : 
 -South-east (se)
 -South-west (sw)
 -West (w)
 -East (e)
 -North West (nw)
 -North East (ne)

This determines the starting direction of the pattern, so writing <sw *> would make the pattern start in the southwestern direction.


Movement Keys. Since patterns can be written in any starting direction, we do not use the previous system, we have 5 keys that determine the relative next direction of the pattern. Think of it like making a road, when you are on the road you want to create a soft left turn but on a map you made a turn from the east to the south-eastern direction.
Anyways, here are the 5 possible movements :
 -Hard turn Left (a)
 -Soft turn Left (q)
 -Forward (w)
 -Soft turn Right (e)
 -Hard Turn Right (d)

 This is very complicated but to see better, imagine that the s key on your keyboard is the first point of the next line and that the Q->D Keys represent the next direction. As i said, you will see the road as if it were on a map but you have to turn like if you were on a road.


 Note on the "spells can be written in any starting direction" comment : 

 by that I meant that <nw qaq>:"nw qaq"  has the same effect as <e qaq> "e qaq" because their movement keys are the same
